jobs.title: SDET Senior Test Lead
jobs.description: Job Summary We are looking for an experienced QA Engineer with a strong background in both functional and automated testing, and a working understanding of AI and machine learning concepts. This role is central to ensuring the quality, reliability, and trustworthiness of enterprise-grade AI solutions — spanning traditional ML models, Generative AI applications, RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, and the data pipelines that power them. This is not a generic QA role. The ideal candidate understands how AI systems behave differently from traditional software — where outputs are probabilistic rather than deterministic, where correctness is contextual, and where testing strategies must account for model drift, hallucination, retrieval quality, and data integrity. You will work alongside AI Engineers, data engineers, and architects to define test strategies, build validation frameworks, and deliver clear, actionable quality reports to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Key Responsibilities Functional Testing • Design, execute, and maintain comprehensive test plans and test cases for AI/ML solutions, Generative AI applications, RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, and supporting REST APIs. • Validate end-to-end functional behaviour of AI and its integrated solutions against defined acceptance criteria and business requirements. • Test ML model outputs for correctness, consistency, and alignment with expected behaviour — including classification results, predictions, anomaly flags, and recommendations. • Evaluate RAG pipeline quality: validate retrieval relevance, chunking effectiveness, reranking behaviour, hybrid search results, and the accuracy of LLM-generated responses against source documents. • Test agentic AI workflows for correct tool/function invocation, reasoning logic, multi-step task completion, and appropriate handling of edge cases and failures. • Conduct API testing to validate request/response behaviour, error handling, authentication, input validation, and performance under load. Official Use Only • Perform data pipeline testing: validate data ingestion, transformation, cleansing, and output quality across batch and streaming workflows. • Execute regression testing following model updates, pipeline changes, or infrastructure modifications. • Test non-functional requirements including latency, throughput, scalability, and resilience. • Conduct exploratory testing to surface unexpected or emergent behaviours in AI systems — particularly in agentic and LLM-based solutions. Test Automation • Design and implement automated test frameworks and suites for AI solutions, APIs, and data pipelines. • Build reusable, maintainable automation scripts in Python, integrating with testing frameworks such as pytest, Robot Framework, or equivalent. • Develop automated regression suites that can be integrated into CI/CD pipelines to enable continuous quality validation. • Implement automated evaluation pipelines for Generative AI outputs — including LLM-as-judge scoring, semantic similarity checks, factual grounding validation, and response consistency testing. • Automate data quality checks within Databricks or equivalent pipeline environments to validate schema, completeness, referential integrity, and statistical distributions. • Integrate test automation with monitoring and alerting tools to detect quality degradation in deployed AI solutions. AI-Specific Validation • Evaluate LLM outputs for hallucination, factual accuracy, relevance, coherence, and adherence to safety and content guidelines. • Validate embedding quality, vector search precision/recall, and metadata filtering behaviour in RAG architectures. • Test model fairness, consistency, and robustness across diverse inputs, including adversarial and edge-case scenarios. • Validate that responsible AI principles — including content safety filters, guardrails, and bias mitigations — are functioning as designed. Official Use Only • Support model drift monitoring by defining baseline benchmarks and alerting thresholds for deployed ML models. Reporting & Stakeholder Communication • Produce clear, well-structured test reports summarizing test coverage, results, defect trends, quality risks, and recommendations — tailored for both technical and non-technical audiences. • Maintain dashboards and metrics that provide ongoing visibility into solution quality, test execution progress, and open defects. • Document defects clearly, with reproducible steps, expected vs. actual behavior, severity assessment, and supporting evidence (logs, screenshots, sample data). Skill Requirements Functional Testing Proven experience in functional, integration, regression, and exploratory testing of complex software systems. Strong ability to analyse requirements, design test strategies, and write high-quality test cases with clear pass/fail criteria. Experience testing REST APIs using tools such as Postman, REST Assured, or equivalent. Familiarity with testing data-intensive applications, including validation of pipeline outputs and structured/unstructured data quality. Experience working in Agile/Scrum delivery environments, including sprint-based test planning and execution. Test Automation Hands-on experience building and maintaining automated test suites using Python-based frameworks (pytest preferred). Official Use Only Experience integrating test automation into CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, or equivalent). Ability to write clean, maintainable automation code following good software engineering practices. Experience with API test automation and data validation automation. AI & Domain Knowledge Working knowledge of AI and ML concepts: understanding of how models are trained, evaluated, and deployed — and the implications for testing strategies. Familiarity with Generative AI concepts: LLMs, RAG pipelines, embeddings, vector search, chunking, reranking, and agentic workflows. Ability to evaluate LLM output quality, including identifying hallucinations, factual errors, relevance gaps, and unsafe content. Understanding of AI non-determinism and how to design testing approaches that account for probabilistic outputs (e.g., semantic equivalence checks rather than exact string matching). Awareness of responsible AI principles: content safety, bias, fairness, and transparency. Reporting & Communication Strong written communication skills, with the ability to produce clear, professional test reports and defect documentation. Ability to distil technical quality findings into concise summaries suitable for non-technical stakeholders. Experience maintaining test metrics and quality dashboards — using tools such as Azure DevOps, Jira, Confluence, or equivalent. Comfortable presenting quality status and risks in team meetings and sprint ceremonies. Tools & Platform Familiarity Familiarity with Azure cloud services relevant to AI solutions: Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Search, Azure Databricks, and ADLS — sufficient to understand system architecture and design targeted test scenarios. Experience with version control (Git) and collaborative development workflows. Familiarity with logging and observability tools (e.g., Azure Application Insights) to support defect investigation and root cause analysis. Must Have Skill API Testing,Selenium,Software Development Engineer in Test (SDET) Good to Have Skill Other Requirements Nice to Have Hands-on experience with LLM evaluation frameworks such as RAGAS, DeepEval, or LLM-as-judge implementations. Experience with performance/load testing tools (e.g., Locust, k6, or Azure Load Testing). Exposure to Databricks notebooks or PySpark for data pipeline validation. Experience testing ML model fairness and bias using tools such as Fairlearn or equivalent. ISTQB certification or equivalent formal QA qualification. Experience in a data engineering or AI engineering adjacent role — providing deeper empathy for the systems being tested.

jobs.description: DESCRIPTION Alexa+ is Amazon’s next-generation, AI-powered virtual assistant. Building on the original Alexa, it uses generative AI to deliver a more conversational, personalised, and effective experience. Alexa Sensitive Content Intelligence (ASCI) team is developing responsible AI (RAI) solutions for Alexa+, empowering it to provide useful information responsibly. The Mission Build AI safety systems that protect millions of Alexa customers every day. As conversational AI evolves, you'll solve challenging problems in Responsible AI by ensuring LLMs provide safe, trustworthy responses, building AI systems that understand nuanced human values across cultures, and maintaining customer trust at scale. What You'll Build You'll pioneer breakthrough solutions in Responsible AI at Amazon's scale. Imagine training models that set new safety standards, designing automated testing systems that hunt for vulnerabilities before they surface, and certifying the systems that power millions of daily conversations. You'll create intelligent evaluation systems that judge responses with human-level insight, build models that truly understand what makes interactions safe and delightful, and craft feedback mechanisms that help Alexa+ grasp the nuances of complex customer conversations. Here's where it gets even more exciting: you'll build AI agents that act as your team's safety net—automatically detecting and fixing production issues in real-time, often before anyone notices there was a problem. Your innovations won't just improve Alexa+; they'll fundamentally shape how it learns, evolves, and earns customer trust. As Alexa+ continues to delight customers, your work ensures it becomes more trustworthy, safer, and deeply aligned with customer needs and expectations. Your work directly protects customer trust at Amazon's scale. Every innovation you create—from novel safety mechanisms to sophisticated evaluation techniques—shapes how millions of people interact with AI confidently. You're not just building products; you're defining industry standards for responsible AI. This is frontier research with immediate real-world impact. You'll tackle problems that require innovative solutions: training models that remain truthful and grounded across diverse contexts, building reward models that capture the nuanced spectrum of human values across cultures and languages, and creating automated systems that continuously discover and address potential issues before customers encounter them. You'll collaborate with world-class scientists, product managers, and engineers to transform state-of-the-art ideas into production systems serving millions. What We're Looking For Deep expertise in state-of-the-art NLP, Large Language Models Track record of building scalable ML systems Passion for impactful research—where frontier science meets real-world responsibility at scale Excitement about solving problems that will shape the future of AI Ready to work on AI safety challenges that define the industry? Join us. Key job responsibilities The Responsible AI (RAI) team is at the forefront of building AI systems that are safe, ethical, and trustworthy. As a Senior Applied Scientist, you'll lead the scientific vision for end-to-end Responsible AI solutions—pioneering algorithms that eliminate false information, designing frameworks that hunt down vulnerabilities before bad actors find them, and developing models that understand human values across every culture we serve. Working alongside world-class engineers and scientists, you'll push the boundaries of model training, building agentic AI systems that coordinate multiple autonomous agents to solve complex safety challenges—transforming bold research into production systems that protect millions of customers daily while withstanding attacks and delivering exceptional experiences. But here's what makes this role truly special: you'll shape the future. You'll lead efforts to identify, define, and mitigate risks early—protecting customers before they're impacted—and mentor the next generation of AI safety experts. You'll design multi-agent architectures where distributed AI systems exhibit emergent collective intelligence while maintaining human oversight and control. Every innovation you drive—from consensus-driven reasoning frameworks to sophisticated orchestration patterns—will set new standards for trustworthy AI at the world's largest scale. A day in the life As a Responsible AI Scientist, you're at the frontier of AI safety—experimenting with breakthrough techniques that push the boundaries of what's possible. You partner with engineering to transform research into production-ready solutions, tackling complex optimization challenges. You brainstorm with Product teams, translating ambitious visions into concrete objectives that drive real impact. Your expertise shapes critical deployment decisions as you review impactful work and guide go/no-go calls. You mentor the next generation of AI safety leaders, watching ideas spark and capabilities grow. This is where science meets impact—building AI that's not just intelligent, but trustworthy and aligned with human values. About the team Our team pioneers Responsible AI for conversational assistants. We ensure Alexa delivers safe, trustworthy experiences across all devices, modalities, and languages worldwide. We work on frontier AI safety challenges—and we're looking for scientists who want to help shape the future of trustworthy AI. jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer, Prime Video Commerce Tech
jobs.description: DESCRIPTION When a customer opens Prime Video anywhere in the world - on a Fire TV in Mumbai, a phone in Tokyo, a browser in Berlin - a commerce system determines if they are entitled to watch a content, what it costs, and how they pay. That system is ours. The Prime Video Commerce team in Bengaluru owns the offers and payments transaction path for hundreds of millions of customers globally. We process millions of requests per second across high double-digit countries, spanning every device type, multiple currencies, and dozens of payment methods - with four-nines availability targets. We support the full spectrum of Prime Video monetisation: ad-free and ad-enabled subscriptions, transactional purchases and rentals, channel subscriptions, with how we pay for them – every payment method in a country, and payment type – at once, in installments. This is not a role where the architecture is settled, and you maintain it. We are at an inflection point - evolving from product-line silos into a unified orchestration platform, decoupling payment logic from the commerce stack, closing the gap to four-nines availability, and shaping what comes next: better support for an agent interaction, better pricing rules and so on. We are hiring a Principal Engineer to own the end-to-end technical vision across both Offers and Payments, because a customer discovering an offer, selecting it, and completing payment is one continuous flow — and the leader who resolves the architectural fragmentation must span domains and Amazon verticals. Key job responsibilities Lead the technical direction for the commerce platform’s offer-to-payment architecture, making critical decisions on system design, service boundaries, and data contracts for performance, scalability, and resilience at millions of TPS Define and drive a multi-year architecture transformation – to improve resiliency, monitorability, and to deliver flexibility and speed Be Hands on to deliver goals tracked at the Amazon executive bench level Drive innovation in AI/GenAI-powered commerce - designing agent-callable service interfaces, AI-native development workflows, and intelligent decision making systems Collaborate across multiple organizations to align technical vision and priorities, influencing decisions at VP level & above without direct authority Define best practices for system architecture, operational excellence, and engineering processes — maintaining high standards for software quality, availability, and cost efficiency Mentor and develop senior engineers toward Principal-level scope, fostering technical growth through design reviews, architecture guidance, and hands-on pairing Lead engineering efforts that directly improve customer experience — reducing transaction failures, improving latency, and enabling commerce at global scale Establish and champion AI-native engineering practices across the organisation, including spec-driven development, GenAI-assisted automation, and AI-powered operational tooling A day in the life Your days are varied - and that’s the point. This role sits at the intersection of deep technical work, delivery of business goals, organizational influence, and talent development. On any given week, you might be writing a technical vision document that dozens of engineers will build against; sitting with a fellow engineer to walk through a design and build their confidence to own bigger problems; challenges customer experiences we build; leading an architecture review where three teams with competing constraints need to converge on a shared interface; deep-diving into a production incident to identify the systemic pattern and design the architecture that prevents the entire class of failure; or prototyping a proof-of-concept that validates a critical architectural assumption before the team invests months of execution. You hold a high technical bar and an equally high bar for how you treat people. You operate across time zones with genuine empathy. You’re as comfortable whiteboarding a distributed systems problem as you are coaching someone through a difficult career conversation. You don’t just set direction — you make the people around you capable of carrying it forward without you. About the team We are the Prime Video Commerce Offers team in Bengaluru — engineers across all levels and managers who build and own the commerce experiences that customers across the globe interact with every day. We're proud of what we've built, and we're just getting started. We are a worldwide team, and we operate like one. That means working across time zones with genuine empathy — understanding that your counterpart in Seattle or London has a life outside of work, just as you do, and that great collaboration doesn't require anyone to sacrifice their personal time. Inclusivity isn't a value we list on a slide — it's how we work. We believe the best ideas come from diverse perspectives, and we actively create space for every voice to be heard, regardless of level, background, or tenure. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS 12+ years of software development experience with deep expertise in distributed systems Track record of leading architecture transformations across multiple teams and services (not just designing — driving adoption) Experience operating systems at large scale (millions of TPS) with high availability Demonstrated ability to influence without authority across organizational boundaries Hands-on practitioner: you write code, review designs, and prototype — not just govern from a distance Experience with service-oriented architecture evolution (decomposition, interface harmonization, platform building) PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Commerce, payments, or subscription systems at global scale (multi-currency, multi-territory, regulatory complexity) Hands-on experience with AI/GenAI — both as a development practice (AI-native SDLC) and as a system capability (agent-callable services, intelligent decision making) Experience with resiliency engineering (graceful degradation, blast-radius isolation, chaos testing) Track record of mentoring senior engineers toward Principal-level scope and judgment Rapid experimentation: building simulation/forecasting frameworks or ML-driven recommendation systems International expansion experience (local payment methods, regulatory compliance, market-specific adaptation) Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. jobs.title: Database Reliability Engineer/Database Engineer (Rubrik Security Cloud Platform)
jobs.description: About the Role We are seeking an experienced Database Reliability Engineer to own the reliability, performance, and scalability of our end-to-end database infrastructure. You will manage both our low-latency transactional engines and our real-time analytical/lakehouse storage systems. You will bridge systems engineering, database internals, and automation to maintain rock-solid data integrity, low query latency, and high availability across the entire data lifecycle. What you'll do Performance & Query Optimization: Diagnose and resolve latency regressions, lock/latch contention, index strategies, and memory/disk bottlenecks across both row-oriented and columnar engines. Disaster Recovery & Data Integrity: Ensure strict RTO/RPO adherence, automated backup validation, PITR (point-in-time recovery), and data consistency across transactional and analytical stores. Storage Optimization & Compaction: Manage compaction policies, partition strategies, file sizing, and storage tiering to minimize storage costs and read amplification. Transactional Reliability & Operations: Manage HA, automated failover, replication topology, and zero-downtime maintenance for production RDBMS clusters. Analytical Storage Infrastructure: Maintain, scale, and optimize real-time analytical engines (ClickHouse) and lakehouse formats/engines (Apache Iceberg, BigQuery). Infrastructure as Code & Observability: Build declarative automation for cluster provisioning, schema migrations, and metric alerting (Prometheus, PromQL, Grafana) Experience you'll need Database Internals & RDBMS Fundamentals: Deep understanding of ACID guarantees, WAL, checkpointing, and recovery mechanics (e.g., ARIES-style recovery). Comprehensive grasp of concurrency control, transaction isolation levels, lock protocols (2PL, deadlocks), and MVCC architectures. Deep knowledge of storage structures: B+ Trees, LSM-Trees, and columnar storage layouts (e.g., Parquet, ORC, ClickHouse Wide/Compact formats). Operational Database Experience: 4+ years running production database infrastructure, with deep expertise in [PostgreSQL / MySQL]. Experience optimizing and managing cost/quotas in Google Cloud BigQuery (partitioning, clustering, reservation slots). Experience with OLAP DB like: ClickHouse, BQ Systems & Kernel Engineering: Strong Linux fundamentals: I/O subsystems, page cache vs. engine buffer pools, disk alignment, asynchronous I/O, and memory management. Automation & Software Engineering: Using Python or Go for building database automation, operators, and CLI tooling. Experience with Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) and container orchestration. Preferred skills and qualifications Hands-on administration and performance tuning of ClickHouse (cluster topologies, ZooKeeper/Keeper coordination, MergeTree engine family, mutations, and compaction). Experience with change data capture (CDC) pipelines (e.g., Debezium, Kafka) feeding transactional updates into ClickHouse/Iceberg. Experience managing lakehouse storage patterns using Apache Iceberg (metadata management, snapshot expiration, file compaction/orphan cleanup). Experience with automated schema migration tools (e.g., gh-ost, Liquibase, Bytebase). Familiarity with distributed consensus engines ( ClickHouse Keeper,Raft, Paxos). Join Us in Securing and Accelerating the World's AI Transformation Rubrik (NYSE: RBRK) is the Security and AI Operations Company, delivering one platform built at the intersection of data, identity, and AI. The platform enables agentic cyber resilience and trusted AI operations for enterprises worldwide, built to recover before disruption strikes and stay a step ahead, so security is never the reason ambition stalls. jobs.title: Associate Director, Data, Knowledge & Agentic AI Engineering
jobs.description: About the Role GSK R&D and Digital & Tech's collective goal is to deliver GSK impact, including the acceleration of the discovery and development of medicines and vaccines to patients. The Labs and CMC Tech function is central to this mission, driving the reimagining and business transformation of our global laboratory and CMC processes. We are actively transitioning from managing raw scientific data to generating structural scientific knowledge—the foundation for how R&D will discover future medicines in a technology-enabled ecosystem. The Labs CMC Data, Agentic and Knowledge Engineering (DAKE) group architects the data, agentic and knowledge foundations upon which critical R&D processes and scientific workflows depend. Crucially, our operating model relies on a hybrid workforce: AI agents function as "digital workers" to execute hands-on engineering tasks. They generate pipelines, test and deploy them, monitor them in production and remediate failures. Reporting into the Director of Data, Knowledge and Agentic AI Engineering, the Associate Director, Data, Knowledge & Agentic AI Engineering, leads the design of production data systems for a team and its domains within Labs & CMC. The role defines the architectural, quality, and governance standards the team and its digital workers apply, leads the team's AI-grade data infrastructure, and mentors junior and mid-level engineers. Why This Role Exists Production System Leadership: Leads the design of production data systems for a Labs & CMC team and its domains, including pipelines that serve multiple downstream consumers and the AI-grade infrastructure beneath them incorporating existing standards and approaches. Defining the Hybrid Workflow: Defines how the team works with digital workers through the architectural standards, quality checks and review patterns their work must meet within our operating model. Capability Mentorship: Improves and implements our engineering standards with respect to code, documentation and governance, and advances mentoring of junior and mid-level engineers. Key Responsibilities Domain-Level Data and Agentic Engineering Design and build production data pipelines for your specific Labs and CMC domain, serving multiple downstream scientific consumers. Implement, enforce and extend our team's patterns for agent-generated work, defining exactly what digital workers build and remediate autonomously versus what requires human review within your domain. Integrate digital workers into your team's specific orchestration and observability workflows, applying clear guardrails, tool designs, and human-in-the-loop controls. Lead the response to significant data quality incidents within your team's purview, from initial detection through to permanent resolution. Context & Semantics Layer Set the context standards for the team's Labs & CMC domains: how definitions, contracts, classification and lineage are captured in the governed context layer, so humans and digital workers can rely on them. Actively contribute to the broader Labs and CMC context layer by feeding your team's hands-on operational experience upward to evolve the platform. Data Quality & Governance Execute data quality and governance standards for your team's domains, encoding them directly into the context layer so both humans and digital workers apply them by default. Lead local data quality initiatives to achieve measurable outcomes, such as reduced error rates, improved audit readiness, and better downstream AI performance. AI Data Infrastructure & Lifecycle Extend our AI-grade data infrastructure for your team's specific AI system needs, including novel retrieval architectures, improved real-time data flows, and smart evaluation datasets. Manage the data lifecycle for AI systems within your domain, including versioning, drift monitoring, and the governance of AI artefacts. Platform Engineering & Mentorship Design cloud data infrastructure for your team's domains, improve our Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and its deployment reliability. Build shared platform components used by multiple engineers and digital workers to reduce setup time for new Labs and CMC data projects. Set and enforce the code and documentation quality standards for your team, written explicitly for a hybrid workforce of humans and digital workers Mentor junior and mid-level engineers through pairing, code review, and direct feedback to visibly improve their capability and independence. Basic Qualifications 8+ years of data engineering experience, including significant time leading the design and operation of complex production data systems. Deep expertise with modern warehouses or lakehouses, orchestration and transformation frameworks, and batch and streaming architectures. Demonstrated experience designing and operating AI agents or substantial LLM-powered tools inside data engineering workflows, including tool design, evaluation, observability and human-in-the-loop controls. Experience leading the design of AI-grade data infrastructure for production AI systems, including evaluation datasets, retrieval architectures and real-time data flows. Experience leading data lifecycle management for AI systems, including versioning, drift monitoring and governance of AI artefacts. A track record of defining data quality and governance standards for a team or domain that others adopted, with measurable outcomes. Experience leading cloud data infrastructure design with infrastructure as code. Preferred Qualifications Technical lead for one or more data platforms or significant domains, from first build through to scale. Experience with catalogue, metadata, semantic or lineage infrastructure that AI systems consume. Experience working within highly regulated industries, such as life sciences, where strict data integrity and auditability are non-negotiable mandates. Education Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Data Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Skills Computer Programming, Data Analysis, Data Architecture Development, Databricks Unified Data Analytics Platform, Data Engineering, Data Governance, Data Ingestion, Data Integration, Data Migrations, Data Modeling, Data Transformation, ETL Development, Performance Optimizations, Performance Tuning, Structured Query Language (SQL) Why GSK? Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale. People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people. jobs.title: Engineer II, Data Engineer
jobs.description: About the Role: Enterprise AI (EAI) builds the data foundations that GSK's AI systems depend on. In our operating model, digital workers do the hands-on data engineering. They generate pipelines, test and deploy them, monitor them in production and remediate failures. Our engineers direct that work and own the quality of what ships. Humans and digital workers both rely on a governed context layer. It makes data, meaning, permissions and history retrievable at the moment they are needed, and sits above our data platforms and beneath every experience and agent built on them. The Data Engineer II independently owns a data domain. The role designs pipelines for complex use cases, owns the quality of what digital workers deliver in that domain, and keeps its context accurate and audit-ready. It also contributes reusable components to the platform and raises technical quality across the team. Why This Role Exists: Owns a data domain end-to-end, with clear accountability for the pipelines, models and datasets digital workers build and operate in it, and sound independent judgement on design choices. Makes digital workers more effective in that domain by improving the frameworks, tools and evaluations they use, so manual intervention falls measurably over time. Delivers quality-assured data to AI systems through data contracts, governed context and quality frameworks that hold up to audit. Key Responsibilities: Agent-Operated Data Engineering: Design pipelines for complex use cases and direct digital workers to build and operate them, with clear, defensible architectural trade-offs. Own the quality of agent-generated work in your domain: review, test and approve it within the remit EAI's operating model sets, and escalate what falls outside it. Improve how digital workers operate in your domain by refining the frameworks, tools and evaluations they use, iterating on reliability signals so manual intervention falls measurably over time. Context & Semantics: Own the context for your domain in the governed context layer: definitions, contracts, lineage and governance documentation that humans and digital workers rely on. Contribute reusable components to the context layer, such as metadata enrichment, classification or lineage capture, that other domains can adopt. Data Quality & Governance: Build an end-to-end data quality framework for your domain, with lineage tracking and governance documentation that passes audit. Apply privacy and consent controls in AI data pipelines and manage PII appropriately across the data lifecycle. AI Data Infrastructure & Lifecycle: Design and build feature stores, vector databases or retrieval infrastructure for production AI systems, with data contracts that give each AI consumer consistent, quality-assured inputs. Manage training datasets, evaluation sets and data versioning for AI projects in production, and contribute to evaluation dataset design with a clear view of how data decisions affect model quality. Platform & Infrastructure: Build cloud data infrastructure independently using infrastructure as code and contribute reusable components to the team's data platform. Design observability into pipelines from the start and resolve infrastructure issues with minimal disruption to consumers. Own incident response for your domain, with clear post-incident analysis and follow-through. Collaboration & Standards: Raise team technical quality through code review and documentation, with specific improvements to shared practices. Preferred Experience: Led the design and delivery of a component of a larger data platform. Experience with agentic systems in production: multi-step tool use, evaluations, guardrails and observability applied to operational data problems. jobs.title: Associate, AI Data Scientist- Private Markets
jobs.description: Location: Bengaluru, Karnataka Team: Data Science Job Requisition #: R264031 Date posted: Nov. 02, 2026 Job description About this role Build efficient, trusted agentic AI for private-markets intelligence Research, build and scale advanced agentic systems and fit-for-purpose language models that turn complex information into dependable data, research and decision intelligence. Your team You will join a multidisciplinary AI and data science team focused on applying advanced AI to high-value challenges in private markets. The team brings together data science, engineering, product and domain expertise, and works closely with users to develop practical capabilities that improve how information is acquired, researched and managed. You will work in an environment where applied research is expected to become dependable production capability. We value intellectual curiosity, rigorous experimentation, strong engineering and responsible AI, with quality, security and appropriate human oversight designed in from the start. Your role & impact As an Associate, AI Data Scientist, you will be a hands-on technical contributor responsible for researching, building and scaling enterprise-grade agentic AI capabilities. Working directly with users and senior technical leaders, you will translate complex private-markets workflows into well-evaluated systems that move from experimentation to governed production and sustained adoption. Your core mandate is to advance multi-agent LLM systems through effective agent design patterns, rigorous evaluation and disciplined model engineering. You will develop workflows that plan, retrieve, reason, use tools, verify and escalate appropriately, while selecting the simplest architecture and model that can meet the required quality, latency, cost and control objectives. You will also help establish the lifecycle for open-source small language models and LLMs, from model discovery and benchmarking through training, adaptation, fine-tuning, deployment, monitoring and retirement. Your impact will be visible in stronger data quality, faster research, scalable automation and reusable AI capabilities that help BlackRock Preqin remain at the forefront of private-markets data and technology. Your responsibilities Work forward-deployed with researchers, data specialists and product teams to understand workflows, frame ambiguous problems, define measurable outcomes and iterate rapidly from evidence to production. Research, design and deliver agentic workflows spanning planning, retrieval, tool use, structured extraction, reasoning, verification, exception handling and human escalation, using single-agent or multi-agent patterns where each is demonstrably appropriate. Engineer advanced agent patterns, including bounded iterative loops, reflection and critique, planner-executor and evaluator-optimizer patterns, with explicit stop conditions, budgets and safeguards that prevent unproductive or uncontrolled execution. Build agent and model harnesses that standardise tool interfaces, context assembly, state and memory handling, policy enforcement, tracing, replay and failure recovery. Determine when an agentic architecture, retrieval workflow, specialised model or deterministic service is the best fit, and validate the decision against representative tasks and simpler baselines. Design safe caching and reuse across retrieval, prompts, model responses, tool results and intermediate agent state, with clear cache keys, invalidation, freshness, access-control and provenance requirements. Build systematic evaluation harnesses using representative datasets, explicit quality dimensions, adversarial and edge-case testing, regression suites, human feedback and monitored production outcomes. Research and benchmark open-source SLMs and LLMs for task fit, considering quality, inference performance, cost, licensing, security, deployment constraints and operational supportability; apply fit-for-purpose routing and batching where they improve efficiency. Develop model-adaptation strategies using prompt and context optimisation, supervised fine-tuning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning or other suitable techniques, supported by governed dataset creation, experiment tracking, reproducibility and controlled promotion criteria. Operate the lifecycle for trained and fine-tuned open-source models, including data and model versioning, lineage, experiment and artifact management, evaluation gates, registry and release controls, deployment, performance and drift monitoring, rollback, retraining triggers and retirement. Build production-quality Python components that integrate models with enterprise data, retrieval services, APIs, workflow orchestration and human-review experiences. Improve grounding and trust through attribution, provenance, uncertainty handling, validation checks, access controls and clear separation of source evidence from model-generated conclusions. Own delivered reliability across testing, observability, latency, cost and maintainability, and diagnose model, data, prompt and orchestration failures in production. Document findings, reusable patterns and trade-offs; contribute to design reviews; and communicate results clearly to research, product, engineering, risk and senior stakeholders. Partner with engineering, product, risk, privacy, information security, legal and compliance colleagues to support responsible, secure and accountable use of AI. Required experience We are looking for a hands-on applied AI practitioner who combines strong research and modelling skills with production judgment and user-focused problem solving. You should bring: Strong experience building and deploying AI or machine-learning systems in an enterprise, SaaS, data-product or similarly complex environment, with evidence of taking work beyond prototypes. Practical depth in LLM applications and agentic systems, including retrieval, tool use, planning, orchestration, memory or state management, structured outputs, verification and evaluation of non-deterministic behaviour. Experience implementing and comparing bounded loops, reflection or critique, planner-executor and evaluator-optimizer patterns against simpler baselines, with measurable treatment of quality, reliability, latency, token usage, cost and failure modes. Experience building agent or model harnesses across tool interfaces, context and state management, orchestration, policy enforcement, testing, tracing, replay, deployment and observability. Hands-on experience evaluating, selecting, training or adapting open-source SLMs or LLMs, including benchmarking, governed dataset preparation, supervised or parameter-efficient fine-tuning and inference optimisation. Practical ModelOps experience for trained or fine-tuned models, including dataset and model lineage, experiment and artifact tracking, registries, evaluation gates, controlled release, performance and drift monitoring, rollback, retraining and retirement. Experience designing model routing, batching and safe caching with appropriate keying, invalidation, freshness, privacy, access-control and provenance safeguards. Strong grounding in modern machine learning, experimentation and statistical evaluation, with disciplined handling of train-test separation, leakage, uncertainty, reproducibility and model comparison. Ability to write production-quality Python and work effectively across data preparation, model development, APIs, orchestration, testing, deployment and observability. Experience with unstructured or multimodal information, semantic retrieval, provenance and data-quality engineering in workflows where domain experts provide ground truth and structured feedback. Experience working directly with users or domain specialists to turn ambiguous needs into usable capabilities and iterate based on observed workflow outcomes. Sound judgment on model and architecture trade-offs across efficacy, efficiency, security, licensing, maintainability and operational risk. Clear communication and collaborative delivery skills, with the ability to explain experiments, limitations and production trade-offs to technical and non-technical audiences. Understanding of private markets, alternative investments, financial data or adjacent institutional-investment workflows is desirable; curiosity and the ability to build domain depth quickly are essential. Commitment to responsible AI, data provenance, privacy, security and meaningful human control in high-trust enterprise workflows. Why this role This is an opportunity to work on consequential AI problems, real user workflows and high standards for trust. You will have meaningful hands-on ownership, direct access to users and the opportunity to turn emerging agent and model techniques into durable capabilities with enterprise reach. Our benefits To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of benefits including a strong retirement plan, tuition reimbursement, comprehensive healthcare, support for working parents and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about. Our hybrid work model BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. Employees are currently required to work at least 4 days in the office per week, with the flexibility to work from home 1 day a week. Some business groups may require more time in the office due to their roles and responsibilities. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock. Guidance on AI use for candidates At BlackRock, AI has long been part of how we work – enhancing decision-making, improving operations, and helping us deliver better outcomes for clients. We encourage candidates to use AI thoughtfully to learn, prepare, and work more effectively; but during our interview process, we want to focus on getting to know you through your own experiences, thinking, and judgment. To support you, we’ve provided guidance (opens in new window) on when and how to use AI during our hiring process so you can approach each step with confidence and showcase your best self. About BlackRock At BlackRock, we are all connected by one mission: to help more and more people experience financial well-being. Our clients, and the people they serve, are saving for retirement, paying for their children’s educations, buying homes and starting businesses. Their investments also help to strengthen the global economy: support businesses small and large; finance infrastructure projects that connect and power cities; and facilitate innovations that drive progress. This mission would not be possible without our smartest investment – the one we make in our employees. It’s why we’re dedicated to creating an environment where our colleagues feel welcomed, valued and supported with networks, benefits and development opportunities to help them thrive. jobs.description: Job Summary As an Agentic Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), you will operate at the critical intersection of deep full-stack engineering, high-level system architecture, and client-facing consulting. You are not just writing code; you are bridging the gap between technical pre-sales and scalable, enterprise-grade production delivery. Embedded directly with enterprise clients, you will act as a primary technical advisor, turning ambiguous, messy business realities into production-ready autonomous and multi-agent systems—collectively known as Business Transformation Agents. At the 8–12 years experience level, you will own the end-to-end system design and architecture of these solutions. You will navigate complex client environments to wrangler disparate data, design robust ETL pipelines, rapidly prototype Proof of Concepts (POCs), and carry them through to highly secure, integrated production ecosystems. Beyond core delivery, you will also play a pivotal role in pursuits, collaborating with account teams on discovery workshops, technical demos, and solution shaping, while leading and mentoring a lean engineering pod. Key Responsibilities Pre-Sales to Production Bridging : Own the transition from rapid conceptual prototyping and discovery POCs to production-grade, highly scalable enterprise deployments, balancing velocity with operational readiness. System Design & Architecture Ownership: Systems Thinking, Define, model, and document the end-to-end architectural views (logical, data flow, integration, security, and operations) of agentic systems within complex enterprise ecosystems. Data Wrangling & ETL Integration: Architect and build ingestion, data modeling, and data pipelines to clean, structure, and orchestrate messy client data from disjointed legacy systems before applying AI/LLM orchestration. Build End-to-End Agentic Solutions : Apply hands-on engineering to design and deploy custom agents. Implement core agentic patterns: prompt/context engineering, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) or context graphs, memory, tool/function calling, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and multi-agent orchestration. Enterprise-Grade Integration : Connect AI agents to existing enterprise legacy databases, ERPs, and cloud environments using secure APIs, OAuth, custom enterprise connectors, and robust identity access management (IAM) controls. Evaluation & Testing Rigor : Establish rigorous testing suites, regression pipelines, and evaluation harnesses to continuously check agent safety, response quality, latency, and operational guardrails. Own AgentOps & Production Telemetry : Build CI/CD, deployment versioning, and real-time observability feedback loops to manage cost, trace errors, and monitor production agent behavior. Technical Leadership & Pod Governance : Set the engineering direction, conduct rigorous code/architecture reviews, mitigate delivery risks, and mentor a lean pod of 3–5 developers to build high-performance, reusable IP. Business Consulting : Prototyping (POC-to-Prod): Transitioning early-stage ideas and pre-sales requirements into secure, high-value, demo-ready POCs. Business interface and driving requirements / ideation with Business/ Running stakeholder discovery sessions, mapping workflows, building business cases. Eventually, Design and deploy Business Transformation Agents with measurable ROI. Also, drive efficiency through reduced cycle times, lower manual effort, and higher accuracy. Skill Requirements Experience : 8–12 years of professional software engineering, system design, or tech consulting experience, demonstrating clear growth from hands-on coding to architectural design and technical team leadership. Architectural & System Design Depth : Proven expertise in designing complex distributed systems, selecting appropriate caching strategies, scaling APIs, and evaluating database trade-offs. Data Engineering & Wrangling Skills : Practical proficiency in SQL, schema design, data modeling, and orchestration pipelines (e.g., handling structured/unstructured client data feeds) to prepare data for downstream AI processing. Advanced Python Engineering : Masterful command of idiomatic, typed, tested, and packaged Python built for robust API services and orchestration. T-Shaped Cloud Experience : Deep, hands-on architectural and deployment experience on at least one major hyperscaler (AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud Platform), with working awareness of patterns, security controls, and configurations across the others. Agentic AI & LLM Fluency : Hands-on experience designing workflows and systems using at least one agent development framework (e.g., LangGraph, CrewAI, Google ADK, OpenAI Agents SDK, Bedrock AgentCore, or Microsoft Semantic Kernel) and multi-LLM platforms. Consulting & Pre-Sales Maturity : Outstanding communication skills with experience facilitating customer discovery workshops, managing client expectations, demonstrating technical feasibility, and shaping solutions for new business pursuits. Engineering & Governance Rigor: Solid understanding of DevSecOps, testing harnesses, and Responsible AI guardrails (auditability, human-in-the-loop triggers, compliance control design). Must Have Skill Automation Anywhere Agentic AI,Digital System Architecture,Extract Transform Load (ETL) Automation,Prototyping (IxD),Marketing/Presales/Sales support Good to Have Skill Evaluation and Assessment Other Requirements What Sets You Apart (Preferred Skills) Fluency across multiple agent frameworks and architectural judgment to select the ideal model/tooling configuration based on specific client constraints. Hands-on experience deploying AI agents onto managed enterprise runtimes (e.g., Vertex AI Agent Engine, Bedrock AgentCore) with active cost-containment and governance patterns. Deep functional domain knowledge in core transformation spaces: Finance operations, procurement, supply chain, HR, insurance claims, customer service, or regulatory compliance. A proven track record of creating reusable code components, utility libraries, or specialized accelerators adopted across wider engineering communities. Broader AI/ML Python ecosystem familiarity (e.g., data prep, feature extraction, evaluation metrics) and comfort collaborating directly with data science specialists. How Success is Measured POC-to-Production Conversion : The efficiency and reliability with which pilot projects/POCs are successfully architecturalized, productionized, and integrated into live environments. Sustained Value Creation : Quantifiable improvements in process cycle-time, manual effort reduction, increased accuracy, and decreased cost-to-serve for the client. Architectural Stability & Security : Zero major security breaches or infrastructure regressions, combined with low exception rates, robust cost-management, and high system availability. Team & Asset Velocity : Successful enablement and mentorship of the local delivery pod, alongside high utilization of reusable internal code accelerators.

jobs.title: Assistant Vice President
jobs.description: Job Description: Key Responsibilities 1. Agentic Solution Architecture & Design Authority Lead discovery and solutioning with stakeholders; translate business objectives into target-state agentic AI architectures, blueprints, and roadmaps . Own end-to-end solution design : multi-agent orchestration, tool-using agents, human-in-the-loop patterns, memory and state management, RAG and knowledge layers, and enterprise integration. Drive build vs. buy vs. partner decisions for models, agent frameworks, and solution with EXL standards. 2. Architecture Standards, Governance & Responsible AI Define and enforce reference architectures, design standards, and reusable patterns for agentic AI solutions across accounts. Embed security, privacy, compliance, and responsible AI – including agent guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and auditability – into every design. Conduct architecture and design reviews , ensuring solutions are scalable, cost-efficient, and production-grade. 3. Technical Leadership Through Delivery Guide Forward Deployment Engineers, data scientists, and delivery teams from design through production – remaining hands-on at critical points (prototyping, integration, performance tuning). De-risk delivery by resolving complex technical blockers : legacy integration, agent reliability, model performance, and latency/cost/quality trade-offs. Ensure solutions move beyond POCs to enterprise-wide adoption and value realization . 4. Stakeholder Engagement & Advisory Act as trusted technical advisor to CIOs, CDOs and enterprise architects; lead architecture workshops, design authority boards, and executive briefings. Support pre-sales and strategic deals : solution shaping, effort estimation, technical proposals, and orals. Articulate architecture decisions in business terms – value, risk, cost, and time-to-market. 5. Capability Building & Reuse Convert engagement learnings into reusable assets, accelerators, and reference implementations for EXL’s agentic AI portfolio. Mentor architects and senior engineers; raise the architecture bar across the Enterprise AI practice. Continuously track and translate emerging AI advances (Agentic AI, LLMs, autonomous systems) into EXL-ready architecture strategies. Technical & Architecture Expertise (Agentic AI) Multi-agent system design : supervisor–worker hierarchies, planner–executor and reflection loops, blackboard and swarm patterns; task decomposition, delegation, and inter-agent communication protocols; deciding when a single-agent vs. multi-agent topology is architecturally justified. Agent state, memory & context engineering : short-term vs. episodic vs. semantic memory design, checkpointing and resumability, durable execution for long-running agents; context-window budgeting, compaction/summarization strategies, and retrieval-augmented context assembly. Framework and protocol depth : LangGraph (graph state machines, interrupts, human-in-the-loop nodes), CrewAI, AutoGen/Semantic Kernel; MCP (Model Context Protocol) for tool and resource federation and A2A for agent interoperability; sound judgment on custom orchestration vs. framework adoption. Model strategy & token economics : model portfolio design and routing (frontier LLMs vs. SLMs), structured outputs and function-calling schema design, constrained decoding; fine-tuning vs. RAG vs. prompt-optimization trade-offs; prompt caching, batching, distillation, and quantization to hit latency and cost SLOs. Retrieval & knowledge architecture : hybrid retrieval (sparse + dense), rerankers, GraphRAG and knowledge graphs; chunking and embedding strategy, freshness pipelines, and access-control-aware retrieval (document/row-level security) for regulated enterprises. Evaluation architecture : golden datasets, LLM-as-judge with calibration, trajectory-level agent evals, regression harnesses wired into CI/CD gates, and online canary/A-B evaluation for continuous quality assurance. Guardrails, safety & governance : prompt-injection and jailbreak defenses, PII detection/redaction, policy engines, sandboxed tool execution, human-approval gates for high-risk actions, and full audit trails/lineage for responsible AI and regulatory compliance. Production & platform architecture : model gateways, multi-tenancy, VPC/private endpoints, HA/DR, autoscaling, rate limiting, and circuit breakers; observability via distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry), token/cost telemetry, and drift monitoring at enterprise scale. Enterprise integration : event-driven and API-led integration patterns, identity propagation (OAuth/OIDC), secrets management, and integrating agents with CRM, contact center, workflow platforms, and legacy estates. Multimodal & emerging stacks : voice agents (streaming ASR/TTS – e.g., ElevenLabs), avatar/video (HeyGen), computer-use agents; fluency with AI-native tooling (Claude Code, Cursor) and evolving OpenAI/Anthropic platform capabilities. Responsibilities: Robust, scalable agentic architectures that move engagements from POC to enterprise-wide production adoption. Reference architectures, patterns, and accelerators reused across multiple accounts – reducing time-to-value and delivery risk. Tangible business outcomes (productivity, cost, quality, revenue) enabled by sound architecture decisions. Strong security, compliance, and responsible AI posture across all designed solutions. Recognized technical credibility with CTO/CIO organizations, contributing to account growth and strategic deal wins. Qualifications: 12+ years of experience in software/solution architecture, data, or digital transformation, with 3+ years architecting AI/LLM or agentic AI solutions . Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field. Proven track record of: Architecting and delivering production AI/GenAI solutions for large enterprise clients Serving as design authority across multiple concurrent engagements or programs Operating in business-facing, consulting, or forward-deployed environments with senior stakeholders Strong understanding of: Agentic AI and LLM architectures , RAG, evaluation, and guardrails Data platforms, cloud, security, and compliance Enterprise integration and legacy modernization Experience engaging with CTOs, CIOs, enterprise architects, and executive stakeholders . Willingness to travel and work onsite at business locations as required.

jobs.description: DESCRIPTION Join Alexa AI - ML Engineering and help power personalized, proactive experiences for hundreds of millions of Alexa customers worldwide. As a Data Engineer II, you will design and own the large-scale data pipelines that turn raw customer-interaction signals into the context and features our personalization and proactive-agent models depend on, working side-by-side with SDEs to shape our data strategy and architecture. You will build and operate ETL/ELT pipelines processing billions of records a day, using AWS big-data services (Glue, EMR, Kinesis, Redshift, DynamoDB) and distributed compute. You will partner with SDEs and applied scientists to define data strategy, contracts, and feature pipelines, and to decide architecture direction together. You will own operational health: data migrations, schema/platform updates, and triage of pipeline tickets, directly supporting the SDE team's work. This is a high-visibility role: the data you deliver, and keep running, directly shapes what Alexa proactively tells customers, and when. Key job responsibilities 1. Partner closely with SDEs to help define data strategy, architecture direction, and the long-term roadmap for the team's data platform. 2. Design, build, and own ETL/ELT pipelines that ingest, transform, and load customer-interaction and context data at a scale of billions of records per day. 3. Own operational items end-to-end: data migrations, schema and platform updates, and triage/resolution of data-pipeline tickets, providing day-to-day support to the SDE team. 4. Partner with applied scientists and ML engineers to define data contracts, feature pipelines, and data-quality checks feeding personalization and proactive-agent models. 5. Operate and continuously improve production pipelines: optimize data delivery, redesign for scalability, manage deployments, and drive root-cause fixes for pipeline incidents. 6. Establish and document best practices for data modeling, warehousing, and pipeline design across the team. A day in the life You'll join SDEs in a design discussion to shape data strategy and architecture, then pick up a migration or platform-update ticket and see it through to resolution. You'll trace a data-quality issue in a personalization feature pipeline, support SDEs with any operational asks on your pipelines, and monitor the health of systems processing billions of daily customer-interaction events. You'll partner with applied scientists to onboard new signal sources and triage pipeline alerts. About the team Alexa AI - ML Engineering builds the personalization and proactive-intelligence systems that let Alexa anticipate what customers need before they ask. Data Engineers work side-by-side with SDEs and applied scientists, combining data strategy and large-scale engineering to turn billions of daily customer-interaction signals into the context, features, and content that drive Alexa's ranking, personalization, and proactive-agent experiences. We value ownership, data quality, and working backwards from the customer. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS 3+ years of data engineering experience 4+ years of SQL experience Experience with data modeling, warehousing and building ETL pipelines PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Experience with AWS technologies like Redshift, S3, AWS Glue, EMR, Kinesis, FireHose, Lambda, and IAM roles and permissions Experience with non-relational databases / data stores (object storage, document or key-value stores, graph databases, column-family databases) Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. Develop trusted relationships and technical champions across CTOs, CIOs, CISOs, AI leaders, engineering teams, and other customer stakeholders. Qualify and coordinate support from Deployment Engineering, implementation, training and enablement, product and domain specialists, partners, and other delivery teams. Remain accountable for technical progress and customer outcomes while ensuring delivery teams own implementation execution once engaged. Track adoption, usage, account health, production readiness, and measurable customer impact, intervening early when risks threaten value realization. Apply industry or digital-native expertise to recognize repeatable patterns, sharpen customer priorities, and identify relevant expansion opportunities. Share customer insights with Product, Engineering, and Research, translating field learnings into better products, architecture guidance, and reusable practices. You might thrive in this role if you: Have significant experience in customer-facing technical roles such as solutions architecture, solutions engineering, technical account leadership, AI deployment, or technical customer success. Have guided enterprise organizations from technical evaluation through production adoption and measurable business impact. Bring strong software and cloud architecture foundations, including APIs, distributed systems, data integration, identity, security, and privacy. Understand modern AI systems, frontier LLM models, agentic applications, model evaluation, retrieval, or enterprise AI workflows. Can prototype, explain technical tradeoffs, and work confidently with APIs, SDKs, and languages such as Python or JavaScript. Exercise sound judgment about when to go deep personally, when to involve specialists, and how to define clear handoffs and ownership. jobs.title: LLM & Agentic AI Performance Engineer
jobs.description: Job Details: Job Description: The Role and Impact: Join Intel's Data Center AI organization and help shape how LLM and Agentic AI workloads perform on Intel platforms. Our team operates at a unique intersection of core performance optimization, AI frameworks, and customer-facing AI solutions. We bridge the gap between teams that deeply understand silicon and benchmarking and teams building real-world AI solutions, turning performance insights into software optimizations that developers and customers can use. In this role, you will own end-to-end performance characterization and optimization of LLM and Agentic AI workloads, from Python-level frameworks and inference runtimes down to Linux, system architecture, and hardware performance counters. This is not simply a benchmarking role. Benchmarking tells us what the number is. Your job is to understand why the number is what it is, identify the hardware or software bottleneck, and determine what needs to change to remove it. Your work will translate into code contributions, framework optimizations, best-known configurations (BKCs), customer-ready solutions, and insights that help influence future Intel hardware and software. If you enjoy working across the complete AI stack, from agent frameworks and LLM serving engines to NUMA, memory bandwidth, cache behavior, and silicon counters, this role provides an opportunity to work at that intersection. About the Team: The AI Solutions and Toolkit Engineering team is part of Intel's Data Center organization, focused on enabling modern AI workloads and solutions on Intel platforms. We work across the AI ecosystem, collaborating with AI framework and runtime developers, performance and optimization teams, hardware architects, open-source communities, and solution engineering teams. Our goal is to take deep platform capabilities and performance insights and translate them into practical, optimized AI solutions that developers and customers can deploy. The team works across areas including LLM inference, Agentic AI, AI frameworks and runtimes, workload optimization, open-source software, and datacenter AI systems. Key Responsibilities: Characterize and optimize LLM and Agentic AI workloads across the complete software and hardware stack. Identify performance bottlenecks across AI frameworks, inference runtimes, operating systems, memory, compute, and platform architecture. Design and develop hardware-aware and hardware-agnostic optimizations for AI frameworks and runtimes. Optimize LLM inference techniques including KV-cache management, attention, continuous batching, and quantization. Work hands-on with serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, TGI, or equivalent technologies. Analyze host and accelerator performance using tools such as VTune, EMON/PMU, perf, top-down analysis, and roofline modeling. Debug complex performance issues spanning Python frameworks, native code, Linux, runtime libraries, and hardware. Convert performance findings into software changes, upstream contributions, BKCs, and reusable optimization guidance. Collaborate with open-source communities to upstream and integrate performance improvements. Translate silicon-level findings into actionable recommendations for framework developers, while bringing application and framework insights back to Intel platform and silicon teams. Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications: BE +10 years / M.Tech +8 years in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline. Significant hands-on experience in performance engineering, systems optimization, or workload characterization on server-class platforms. Demonstrated ability to identify complex performance bottlenecks and deliver measurable performance improvements. Strong programming skills in Python and C++, or equivalent systems programming experience in C/Rust. Strong understanding of server architecture including cache hierarchy, memory bandwidth, NUMA, interconnects, and system-level performance behavior. Hands-on experience with Linux performance and system technologies such as affinity, huge pages, cgroups, eBPF, ftrace, perf, or equivalent tools. Preferred Qualifications: Deep understanding of LLM inference, including KV-cache, paged attention, continuous batching and quantization such as INT8, INT4, or FP8. Hands-on experience modifying or optimizing AI serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, TGI, OpenVINO, or equivalent. Experience building, profiling, or optimizing Agentic AI systems using technologies such as LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, MCP-based frameworks, or similar platforms. Experience with hardware counter-level performance analysis using VTune, EMON/PMU, perf, top-down analysis, or roofline modeling. Contributions to significant open-source projects, including upstream code contributions. Ability to communicate across abstraction layers, translating silicon-level findings for software developers and application-level requirements for hardware architects. Why Join This Team? This role gives you the opportunity to work across boundaries that few engineering positions span: Agentic AI & LLMs AI frameworks inference runtimes Linux server architecture silicon You won't be limited to measuring performance or optimizing an isolated component. You'll help connect the entire stack, identify where the real bottlenecks are, implement improvements, and make those optimizations available to developers and customers. The result is tangible: better AI performance today, stronger software solutions for customers, and insights that can influence tomorrow's Intel platforms. As Product Software Engineer II, Reliability Platforms, you will develop features, automation, and tooling for the traffic, compute, and streaming platform layers behind Disney Entertainment & ESPN’s production systems, learning reliability engineering practices while contributing production code to platforms that operate at global scale. You will be part of an organization made up of three complementary teams. Technical Operations is responsible for production readiness and service onboarding, alert response and first-line eyes-on-glass monitoring, defining alerts and thresholds, escalation management, backend capacity management and load testing, and third-layer support for technically complex customer issues. Reliability Platforms is responsible for the traffic, compute, and streaming platform layers, and for the reliability tooling that engineers reliability, resiliency, and self-healing into our production services and automates operational processes. Observability & Platform is responsible for telemetry, instrumentation, and alerting standards, for the internal self-service tooling and automation platforms that enable teams across the organization to deploy, detect, alert, and mitigate in our AWS environments with reliability and velocity, and for the operational data, reliability reporting, and anomaly detection that make those platforms smarter over time. You must understand the demands of managing 24x7 applications at a large scale with well-defined operational objectives. You bring solid development fundamentals and foundational experience across AWS, systems programming, the software development lifecycle, incident response and management, and observability tooling such as Datadog, CloudWatch, and Grafana. Within Reliability Platforms you will take technical direction from the Lead and Sr Product Software Engineers, growing your expertise in reliability engineering, Kubernetes, and observability through pairing, code review, and mentorship.You will report to the Director, Product Software Engineering. jobs.description: Required Experience, minimum: 2 years Required Experience, maximum: 8 years Skills: NOC, LAN, WAN Minimum Qualification: Bachelor of Technology (BTech) Job Purpose NOC L2 Engineers are responsible for carrying out monitoring operations as well configuring network and telecommunication equipment in datacenter and other organizations. Provide 24×7 Level-2 operational support for Data Center, COLO, and Cloud infrastructure by performing advanced incident troubleshooting, service restoration, and operational maintenance. Ensure high availability of network and infrastructure services through proactive monitoring, root cause analysis, timely escalation, and coordination with L1, L3, vendors, and customer teams in accordance with SLA and ITIL processes. Roles & Responsibilities Provide 24×7 Level-2 operational support for Data Center, COLO, and Cloud infrastructure environments. Perform advanced troubleshooting and root cause analysis (RCA) for network, compute, storage, virtualization, and infrastructure incidents. Resolve escalated incidents from NOC L1 within agreed SLA and OLA timelines. Support day-to-day operations of enterprise and Data Center LAN, WAN, Internet, MPLS, VPN, and cloud network connectivity. Configure, troubleshoot, and maintain network devices including routers, switches, firewalls, load balancers, and wireless infrastructure, IB switches. Administer and troubleshoot routing and switching protocols including BGP, OSPF, EIGRP, STP, VLANs, VRRP/HSRP, LACP, and MPLS. Support Data Center Spine-Leaf, VXLAN/EVPN (where applicable), and high-availability network architectures. Support load balancing technologies such as F5 BIG-IP, Radware, NGINX, or equivalent Application Delivery Controllers (ADCs). Monitor infrastructure health, network performance, utilization trends, and service availability using enterprise NMS platforms. Analyze recurring incidents, identify problem trends, and recommend preventive actions. Execute operational runbooks and standard maintenance activities, including software upgrades, patch validation, failover testing, and recovery procedures. Participate in Major Incident Management (MIM), technical bridge calls, and service restoration activities. Coordinate with vendors, OEMs, carriers, cloud providers, and internal engineering teams for issue resolution. Manage Incident, Change, Problem, and Service Request records in accordance with ITIL processes. Maintain technical documentation, Support ISO Audits, operational procedures, network diagrams, and knowledge base articles. Perform capacity monitoring, performance analysis, and infrastructure health assessments. Support planned maintenance activities and validate services before and after implementation. Mentor NOC L1 engineers by providing technical guidance, troubleshooting support, and knowledge transfer. Ensure compliance with operational standards, security policies, and service-level agreements (SLAs). Experience & Educational Requirement BE/B-Tech or equivalent with Computer Science or Electronics & Communication RELEVANT EXPERIENCE 4–7 years of experience in Network Operations, Data Center Operations, or Managed Services environments supporting enterprise and cloud infrastructure. Strong understanding of TCP/IP, LAN/WAN, MPLS, SD-WAN, Routing & Switching, including BGP, OSPF, EIGRP, VLANs, STP, and High Availability protocols. Hands-on experience with enterprise networking platforms such as Cisco, Juniper, Arista, and Data Center switching technologies like, Spine Leaf, Spectrum and InfiniBand. Experience supporting Firewalls, VPNs, Load Balancers (F5 or equivalent), and network security operations. Working knowledge of Windows/Linux administration, DNS, DHCP, NTP, SNMP, Syslog, and network services. Experience with Azure, AWS, or other cloud networking and hybrid Data Center environments. Hands-on experience with Network Monitoring and Observability tools such as SolarWinds, Site24x7, Prometheus, Grafana, Splunk/ELK, Wireshark, or equivalent. Experience using ITSM platforms such as Zoho, ServiceNow, BMC Remedy, Jira Service Management, or equivalent for Incident, Change, and Problem Management. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and Root Cause Analysis (RCA) skills with the ability to resolve complex infrastructure incidents. Strong understanding of Industry security standards like ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, SOC-1&2 Familiarity with scripting or automation using PowerShell, Python, or Bash is desirable. Excellent communication, documentation, stakeholder coordination, and customer service skills. Work in a 24×7 rotational shift environment. Good interpersonal skills and ability to work as a high performing team ITIL Foundation certification (preferred). CCNP Enterprise or equivalent networking certification (preferred). Proficiency in any coding languages (Preferred) Cloud certifications such as Microsoft Azure Administrator Associate, AWS SysOps Administrator, or equivalent are an added advantage. Vendor certifications such as CCNP, RHCSA, Fortinet, Palo Alto, or Splunk are desirable.
